RagShortTexts: Salting or fermenting vegetables extends keeping.
Salt, vessels and storage temperature affect losses.

Variants.Content: Preparing vegetables with salt and storing them in vessels preserves part of the harvest for leaner seasons. Broken pots, scarce salt and poor keeping waste food; preserved vegetables accompany grain and other provisions.
Army vegetables require heavy, breakable vessels and care after opening. They cannot replace staple rations; cooks also need water and room to clean utensils.
Purchasing preserved vegetables includes salt, vessels and carriage. Counting spoiled pots as full rations inflates stores beyond the food actually available.
Households need salt and suitable pots before preserving vegetables. Spoilage loses both produce and work; opening winter stores requires balancing current meals against continued keeping.
